answer: An agent marketplace weights votes by locked collateral, so splitting one deposit among agents named meadow, kernel, and walnut creates no extra voting power. Each unit of collateral can back only one vote at a time, and withdrawals stay locked for 30 days. To control 60% of votes, an attacker must supply 60% of all voting collateral and bear its financing cost throughout the lock; generating thousands of identities adds no influence by itself.
